Both sockets are registered before connection/transfer; failed closes remain registered, active transfers erase their own buffers and decrement in finally, and final close attempts listener/socket cleanup plus executor shutdown/termination and reports outstanding ownership at 1191-1219. findings.title: Failed final completion wait still destroys the route without reaping initiated asynchronous stop work
findings.detail: The final cleanup catches any Exception or Error from awaitActualStop and only appends it to cleanupFailures. It then exits the inner finally, and the outer try-with-resources unconditionally invokes PrivatePgRoute.close. For example, if cleanup polling is interrupted in Thread.sleep at line 1004 while StopWork.send is in flight, this catch proceeds to close the listener and routed sockets at 1195 and shut down the bridges at 1197. StopWork counters do not provide a cancellation or join handle. The production stop/confirmation task was scheduled on CompletableFuture.runAsync and is not owned by bridges, so bridge termination cannot reap it. The same structural gap exists when the final completion wait expires before initiated work finishes.
findings.impact: This path retains the failure honestly but does not satisfy completion before proxy destruction on the failure path. The harness can itself destroy the route while the actual stop task is still sending or is about to run its confirmation transaction, and that task can outlive the case. This is a source-level cleanup ownership gap, not an observed runtime failure or a claim about a held row, pool, primary outage or a general database deadline.
findings.requestedCorrection: Make failure of the completion assertions independent of cleanup/reaping of already initiated stop work. Preserve the primary and wait failures, but retain the route while the actual sender and its confirmation work are observably completed or explicitly cancelled and reaped through owned handles. Do not count a timeout/error or bridge executor termination as completion of the separate task, and do not fabricate CONFIRMED or materialization closure.

evidence.detail: Real caller/relay, reads=1, POST=1, certified received secret, consumed command and resolved RELEASE precede route cut. Direct SELECT 1 remains available; routed fresh connection must produce a causal actual PostgreSQL class-08 exception before caller interrupt. No synthetic SQLException or mock DataSource introduced.

Actual caller must end with CannotCreateTransactionException, causal class-08 driver failure, exactly one fixed suppressed UNKNOWN_OUTCOME/409, restored interrupt, non-null zeroed request/secret arrays and relay disconnection. These assertions precede manual cleanup erasure.

Before rescue the direct observer still requires action DISPATCHING, session ACTING, live materialization, one initial consume command, resolved RELEASE and zero terminal USAGE. Reopen keeps the same port and same routedSource.

Recovery uses actual lease/history for same/new consume keys or exact STALE_FENCE with counts unchanged. No renewal or fabricated authority. Genuine authorized cancellation is separate and requires CANCELLED, UNKNOWN_OUTCOME action and exactly one UNKNOWN_OUTCOME USAGE; later commits are not attributed to the failed helper.
